text:
Your shuttle descends into the young atmosphere of Eochu Bres, through towering battlements of clouds that cast a spray of rain over the viewport which is wiped clean in half a blink by the heat and speed of your descent.
The flight path soon deviates from the general approach corridor which has been ticking off minor use fees from the Tri-Tachyon owned flight control: general volume access fee, priority flight lane fee, service fee, customer satisfaction insurance charge, advertisement bypass fee - you swipe the notifications off and focus on the landscape.

The nav system sounds a tone indicating imminent arrival, and you see Arroyo's private chalet: a small compound of radical geometric architecture surrounded by low outbuildings.
Your shuttle approaches an ellipsoid landing pad that appears to hang in the thin air over a gorge.

Arroyo greets you. He waves off the servants. "I'm glad you came, Captain $playerName." He leads you to one of the bars.

text: You sit at the bar. "This matter is of considerable importance to me. I found some things that predates the first AI War.

With a precise movement, he opens his datapad.
"I was reviewing company archives when I came across an off record site. Gargoyle managed to obtain its coordinates. I want you to go there and bring me anything you find."
"$playerName, can you do this for me? I'll owe you one." Arroyo seems to observe you.
"So, have you reconsidered?"
"I understand."
"Good, I'll log you the coordinates to your datapad."
"Come planetside, I need to look at them."

After a moment you consciously pull your eyes from the pitiless sight, centering your attention on your bridge officers to give your next order.

Cold light begins to grow in the primary display. A subtle pulse begs for your attention.

"Captain, I-" It's your navigation officer, who glances at sensors and receives a nod. "The light is moving. Coming closer."

You consciously pull your eyes from that comfortless light - diminished but not bereft of its call through even the meager medium of the primary display.

It's come to you.

text:
"Aye $playerSirOrMadam! Executing." Sensors barks, then deftly executes a series of overrides. 

Your $shipOrFleet status is up on the central display - shield bubble an unsteady amber, incursions of N-space fissures marked in garish red. A blink of white as active sensors trigger and-

-pressure on the drive bubble spikes, an amber flash, a cacophony of alarms...

* * *

A hidden blackness waiting, lurking, jolts awake. Tendrils lunge eagerly, hungrily, through fissures in the dark behind the night.

"Aye $playerSirOrMadam. Commencing full spectrum sweep." Your Sensors officer acknowledges, voice steady but hands moving with grim certainty, overriding safety interlocks one by one.

The $shipOrFleet glows on the central display, its signature flaring brighter with every passing second. Amber turns to white hot as sensor arrays flood hyperspace with precision pulses along the drive bubble sheath.

For a brief, deceptive moment, the bridge feels calm, controlled even. Protocol followed, procedure executed.

Then the shift comes  imperceptible at first, a thickening of space, a low groan from the inertial compensators. Fissures bloom across the void in malignant red. Power surges climb unchecked.

Beyond the veil, something notices. Hunger stirs, drawn not by accident, but by deliberate signal.
The trial begins. An ancient presence fixes on you, ready and relentless.
Your $shipOrFleet emerges victorious. The incursion collapses and the trial is completed.

You wait.

Alarms are reset, battle restraints engaged. Activity on the bridge gradually quiets as all officers, crew, and systems reach a state of readiness, even anticipation - fight or flight.

The incursions crawl closer to the center of your display volume, expanding unwaveringly and intentionally. 

All eyes are on command interfaces, and all attention is on your next order.

At your command, the unperceived chorus of a multitude of ship systems and machinery dies down with a deepening sigh into muted quietude.

All that remains is the breath and bodies of your bridge crew, a strange assertion of your shared humanity. 

Backup e-lighting, simple chemical things, provide an eerie glow. A series of dimly pulsing commands illuminate your executive interface - a flock of ardent subsystems ready to awaken from minimum operation at your touch.

* * *

A hidden blackness feels the brush of a shadow. Less than a morsel, unworthy of wakefulness. By some analog of distributed instinct a few listless tendrils explore this disturbance, this ripple in the darkness behind the night.
